transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Arjun Rao (Skybridge Hyperion), Selina Morris (Skybridge), Tom Nguyen (Infra Lead), Laila Ibrahim (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Intro, platform fit, infra constraints, action items captured.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — really appreciate you making time. Quick round robin, and then we can jump into what Skybridge is thinking, and then dig into the infra stuff.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Arjun): Thanks Maya — excited. Quick intros from our side: I'm Arjun, I run cloud partnerships at Skybridge Hyperion, Selina is VP Eng, Tom does infra, and Laila handles security/compliance.
00:23 Speaker 3 (Selina): Hi hi.
00:27 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great. Diego, you wanna give a one-liner on what Redwood does for partners?
00:31 Speaker 4 (Diego): Sure — we provide an inference platform for running LLMs across hosted, dedicated pools, and private VPC/on-prem deployments. The thing we bring to a partner like Skybridge is predictable latency and an ops surface for model serving — batching, KV cache, routing, etc.
00:48 Speaker 2 (Arjun): Awesome. High level from our side: Skybridge sells managed GPU clouds focusing on lower-cost, high-density tenancy for inference customers. We want to explore an integration so Redwood can offer a "Skybridge-backed" Dedicated option, and conversely we can list Redwood as a verified runtime for customers.
01:10 Speaker 4 (Diego): Cool. Two quick clarifying q's before we get technical: What GPU SKUs are you primarily offering, and do you support MIG or multi-tenant isolation?
01:21 Speaker 5 (Tom): We're mainly shipping A10G and A30 equivalence — some partners have Ampere A100 clusters and a mix of older T4 fleets for cost tiers. We do experimental MIG slicing on select customers but it's not universal, it's kind of M I G in quotes in our infra.
01:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted. Diego, on Redwood side, primary considerations for Dedicated/private are CUDA/cuDNN versions, our container images, and kernel-level optimizations. We also need to confirm whether we can run our runtime with your node image and whether your scheduler allows pinned affinity.
01:58 Speaker 4 (Diego): Exactly. Also KV cache persistence expectations if customers use long-context workloads, we need stable local storage or a distributed KV to avoid warm-start latency.
02:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): For workloads with long contexts we use prefix caching and optional shared Redis-backed KV in Dedicated — question for Tom: can you expose an NFS/managed redis option across the GPU pools?
02:26 Speaker 5 (Tom): We can expose managed Redis, yes. Network latency between the compute plane and stateful services is usually sub-5ms in region but cross-rack could be higher. We'll send cluster topologies.
02:40 Speaker 2 (Arjun): On the business side, we want to ensure the integration is smooth: minimal image changes, Helm charts, and preferably a test harness so we can validate compatibility before we list it.
02:53 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll provide Helm charts and a compatibility matrix. Diego will take point on the matrix.
03:02 Speaker 6 (Laila): On security, we need to understand data handling for Private deployments. If an enterprise customer picks Private, who holds the keys? HSM? KMS?
03:14 Speaker 4 (Diego): Good Q. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS; we can integrate with your HSM, or you can use our managed KMS for hosted setups. We'll attach the SOC2/ISO docs.
03:27 Speaker 6 (Laila): Also SSO and audit logs — audit retention windows, level of traceability?
03:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): Redwood Console provides token-level tracing and per-route dashboards. We can configure longer retention for enterprise or ship logs to your SIEM; nous — we have APIs for log export.
03:45 Speaker 2 (Arjun): Any restrictions on data residency? Some of our customers require EU-only processing.
03:51 Speaker 4 (Diego): Yes — Redwood supports region pinning and private deployments inside a customer's VPC for residency requirements.
04:02 Speaker 3 (Priya): Diving into runtime details — Tom, what orchestrator are you using? K8s, custom scheduler?
04:08 Speaker 5 (Tom): Kubernetes with a custom scheduler plugin for our pool allocation. We have node labels indicating GPU flavor and tenancy.
04:16 Speaker 4 (Diego): That should be fine. We usually ship as a set of container images with a helm chart for Dedicated and a separate package for Private. Biggest item is nvidia-driver compatibility and kernel modules; we have pre-built images that expect certain CUDA versions.
04:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): Diego, can you call out the supported CUDA/cuDNN combos that are most common?
04:38 Speaker 4 (Diego): Sure — we officially support CUDA 11.7 with cuDNN 8.x for the Ampere line, and CUDA 12.x in experimental branches for Hopper-era. If Skybridge has A100s, we'll need to test CUDA 11.8+; for A30/A10 we can usually work with 11.7.
04:55 Speaker 2 (Arjun): How painful is it to support a mix of versions? Some of our customers still run older stacks.
05:01 Speaker 4 (Diego): It adds overhead but we can support multi-version images via tagged node selectors. That's an ops conversation — Diego: we'll provide a matrix.
05:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): A practical concern: are you comfortable allowing us to run perf micro-benchmarks on a dev slice of your infra? A short smoketest to validate latency/throughput would save time.
05:21 Speaker 5 (Tom): Yes, we can open a dev slice — DM us with the specifics and we'll carve out a pool and give access keys.
05:27 Speaker 6 (Laila): When we do a pilot, we need to ensure logs don't leak tenant data. Will Redwood's telem include PII?
05:36 Speaker 4 (Diego): We redact sensitive user content in logs by default and can configure stricter redaction rules. We'll include a doc on telemetry and PII handling.
05:48 Speaker 2 (Arjun): Competitor question: some partners integrate with Lambda and Paperspace already — what would a customer-facing differentiator be for Skybridge+Redwood?
05:59 Speaker 1 (Maya): Two quick value props: predictable SLOs with dedicated pools + tooling for lowering per-token costs via caching and quantization guidance. Also tighter enterprise features like per-route RBAC and rollout controls for model updates.
06:18 Speaker 2 (Arjun): Sounds good. On the GTM side, we'd want co-branded collateral and a joint verification badge — is that something Redwood does?
06:26 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes — we run a verification program and a partner page; we can draft a joint press template and checklist.
06:33 Speaker 3 (Priya): Technical note: quantization support — do you require specific kernels for int8? That can be painful across driver versions.
06:41 Speaker 4 (Diego): We have quantization friendly kernels but they are sensitive to CUDA/cuDNN combos; we'll call out recommended images. For now, we can run float16 for the smoke test and iterate.
06:54 Speaker 5 (Tom): Regarding tenancy, for the initial pilot we can dedicate nodes rather than rely on MIG — that simplifies isolation and avoids the M I G partitioning issues.
07:02 Speaker 6 (Laila): We also need to discuss contractual stuff. If we do a partner listing, what's the liability model? Data handling? SLAs?
07:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll involve legal — generally partner listings don't change liability; Dedicated/Private contracts can be scoped with SLOs and indemnities. We'll send a standard partner annex.
07:25 Speaker 2 (Arjun): Great. Can we get a timeline for the pilot? Ideally a 4-week smoke test followed by a joint writeup.
07:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): Sounds reasonable. Proposal: Week 1 — compatibility check and access, Week 2 — perf runs, Week 3 — tuning, Week 4 — writeup and decision.
07:45 Speaker 3 (Priya): Diego, I'll need to pair with Tom on the helm values to ensure the runtime configuration map matches his scheduler labels.
07:53 Speaker 5 (Tom): Works for me. I'll share node label conventions and a sample helm values file.
08:00 Speaker 4 (Diego): Also, if you're exposing GPUs via a managed offering, we'll need to know how your autoscaler behaves — cold-start behavior and pre-warm capacity. We have batch-awareness in the runtime but we need to align.
08:14 Speaker 5 (Tom): Autoscaler is aggressive for our multi-tenant pool, but for dedicated slices we can pin capacity. We'll document the scaling windows.
08:25 Speaker 2 (Arjun): Any concerns on the Redwood side about networking or peering? For private VPC deploys we typically require cross-account IAM roles and peering.
08:34 Speaker 4 (Diego): No showstoppers — Redwood Private supports cross-account peering and can run in customer's AWS account. We'll share the VPC diagram and connector steps.
08:47 Speaker 6 (Laila): On compliance, please share encryption at rest details and whether keys are customer-managed. Also want to see pen-test reports.
08:57 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll attach the encryption and pen test summaries. Action item for Maya to share SOC2 and pen test outline.
09:06 Speaker 2 (Arjun): Good. A couple of micro-asks: 1) a short compatibility checklist we can include in our docs, 2) a badge or logo usage guideline.
09:16 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll deliver both.
09:20 Speaker 5 (Tom): For the perf run, what endpoints should we exercise? Chat vs streaming vs embeddings?
09:27 Speaker 4 (Diego): Start with text-generation with 512 token outputs and a standard chat flow with streaming. Also run embedding workloads to measure GPU memory and throughput. We'll provide a sample harness.
09:42 Speaker 3 (Priya): One more note: some of your customers use encrypted local NVMe for KV cache — that will be helpful to keep warm-starts low. Can that be carved out?
09:51 Speaker 5 (Tom): Yes, we can provide encrypted local volumes or a network-backed store depending on the pilot configuration.
10:00 Speaker 2 (Arjun): Sounds like we have a plan. Any blockers we didn't surface?
10:05 Speaker 4 (Diego): From a tech perspective, only the multi CUDA versions and MIG parity might add friction but both seem solvable. From legal/commercial, we'll need partner annex and pilot terms.
10:18 Speaker 6 (Laila): We'll review the SOC2 artifacts and redaction rules; might request a short security questionnaire.
10:26 Speaker 1 (Maya): Totally — send your questionnaire and we'll fill it.
10:30 Speaker 2 (Arjun): Ok, next steps recap?
10:34 Speaker 1 (Maya): Recap, action items: Maya to send SOC2, pen test summary, partner deck; Diego to send driver matrix and sample container images + harness; Tom to provide cluster topology, node labels, and option for dev slice. Arjun to circulate internal stakeholder list and target customers for pilot.
10:58 Speaker 2 (Arjun): Thanks everyone. We'll follow up and schedule the compatibility run.
11:02 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks — talk soon.

End of transcript.
